method: Random generated items re-solved by hand against NCERT Introduction to Psychology (class 11): 4 per chapter file incl. mocks (seed 7, 38 items), 3 per chapter file (seed 11, 27 items), every A-R item keyed 'R is not the explanation' (4) and 3 source-extract items; mock 1 checked for section structure and 70 marks; every fact line, vignette and distinguish pair re-read against the chapters while writing
fixes: source-extract items: an open part (i) drawn from a recall line worded 'Which of these ...' had no options to choose from; such variants are now rejected and regenerated
dropped a 'span of attention = 7 plus or minus 2' recall item (figure not certain in the NCERT framing)
animism item reworded to an unambiguous example (the sun 'goes to sleep')
removed a duplicate key term 'concept' from the memory chapter (kept in Thinking) so subject-wide term stems stay distinct
G. Bose vignette says he worked in psychoanalysis (not 'trained in')
case-based section uses original one-paragraph vignettes (case1 identify, 1 mark; case2 identify and explain, 2 marks) from one deck per subtopic
